source.original_question:
In the figure shown above, if all the water in the rectangular container is poured into the cylinder, the water level rises from $h$ inches to $(h+x)$ inches. Which of the following is the best approximation of the value of $x$ ?
Choices:
A:3
B:3.4
C:3.8
D:4.2

adaptation.new_question:
All marked lengths are in inches. The marked depth of the rectangular container is its water depth. Pouring all this water into the cylinder raises the water level from h to h+x. Which choice best approximates x?
Choices:
A:3
B:3.4
C:3.8
D:4.2
source_visual_changes: Uniform opaque white 768×768 canvas, black 1 pt geometry, prescribed fonts and source-informed labels.

All solid geometry is constructed in true 3D and projected through one frozen camera. Source sketch distortions, decorative lighting and inconsistent hidden-line styles are normalized without weakening the protocol.
The 4-inch mark is explicitly bound to water depth. The diagram retains 3, 6 and 5 as visual conditions; these are not copied into the revised question.

answer_verification.source_answer_conflict: Source drawing leaves a gap above water yet puts 4 beside the container side without dimension endpoints; intended water depth is4. If4 is full containerheight, exact water volume is undetermined.

geometry_notes.material_visibility: Both containers are transparent, as in source. Water-level surfaces are semantic fills; circular boundaries have separately frozen front/back intervals.
